summary: Redwood AE/SE ran a console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for production inference; primary concerns were route-level cost visibility, per-model latency & error trends, and SOC2/KMS for data. Agreed to a pilot with route traffic sharing and a follow-up technical kickoff.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Novaretail), Li Chen (Novaretail), Dana Ortiz (Novaretail finance), Alex (procurement)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. quick agenda, we'll show you the console usage analytics, per-route dashboards and then dig into the cost breakdown.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Hey Jordan, thanks — quick note we're most interested in per-route cost because we have a mix of high-frequency low-latency routes and some big batched embeddings jobs.
[00:30] Priya Nair: Great, that's exactly what the per-route view was built for. i'll share my screen now, bear with me if the network is a little slow.
[00:45] Speaker 1 (screen share blur): (screen popped up) okay console home, we go to Analytics -> Usage.
[01:02] Priya Nair: The top-level chart shows tokens and request counts by model variant, then you can break down by route. here i filtered to the last 14 days. you can see spikes on Nov 4th where you had a marketing campaign, we automatically annotate that if you link events.
[01:25] Li Chen: Hmm that spike is similar to what we saw in our internal telemetry — good to see alignment. question: how accurate are token attributions for streamed responses?
[01:38] Priya Nair: They align to the server-side tokenization we run, minor divergence if you do client-side detokenization. streaming is accounted for by per-chunk usage, so cost is attributed to the request that opened the stream.
[01:55] Dana Ortiz: When you say cost, is this an estimated cost or actual billable? we need numbers finance can reconcile.
[02:07] Jordan Lee: Good question. in the console we show estimated cost by route using current pricing profiles; for Hosted it's the billable. for Dedicated we show estimated unit-cost based on the reserved capacity and the recommended batching/quantization profile.
[02:24] Samir Patel: So for Dedicated, if we reserve N GPUs, the per-token cost we're showing is modelled, not actual invoice line item?
[02:36] Priya Nair: Correct. it's a cost model — we factor in GPU type, utilization, effective throughput with batching, and caching savings. we surface both raw per-token compute cost and the Redwood unit cost after amortizing reservation.
[02:52] [02:52] Speaker 1: (brief crosstalk)
[03:05] Priya Nair: i'll flip to the per-route dashboard. each route is a first-class object in the console — latency percentiles, error rates, tokens per request, and importantly cost per request. you can group routes by product or team.
[03:25] Priya Nair: here's Route: checkout-assistant, 95p latency is 120ms, error rate 0.4%, avg tokens 45, and cost per request $0.0018 on Hosted, projected $0.0007 on Dedicated with current utilization.
[03:42] Li Chen: That delta is helpful. how do you handle KV cache savings? our product uses a lot of repeated prefixes.
[03:55] Priya Nair: We estimate prefix cache hit-rate from real traffic; when cache hits occur we subtract the incremental token compute for the unrolled tokens. admittedly the estimate sometimes undercounts cold-starts — we show a confidence band.
[04:12] Jordan Lee: Also the console shows a toggle to simulate different cache hit rates and batching windows so you can see cost sensitivity.
[04:25] Dana Ortiz: can finance export a monthly per-route cost CSV?
[04:31] Jordan Lee: Yes, there's export — CSV or XLSX. you can also export the raw events for a date range for deeper analysis.
[04:40] Samir Patel: Security — we need to ensure route-level logs don't leak PII and that audit logs are available. where do security logs live?
[04:52] Priya Nair: Audit logs go to your configured destination — you can stream them to S3 or a SIEM with an event-level schema. we offer field-level redaction and optional tokenization on ingest. we also integrate with KMS for envelope keys.
[05:08] Li Chen: Is SSO available? we use SAML with Okta.
[05:12] Jordan Lee: Yes we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC; Priya will drop the security pack after the call.
[05:22] [05:22] Speaker 1: (screen flicker)
[05:30] Priya Nair: Jumping back to cost breakdown — there's a mode that shows per-route unit economics across models. you can pick a route and see model mapping (e.g., gptx-7b-quant -> hosted or dedicated variant).
[05:45] Samir Patel: we have a strict latency SLO of 200ms p95 for checkout flows; i'm worried that batching on Dedicated will hurt us.
[05:57] Priya Nair: Totally understood. the console has a latency SLO simulator: you can set target p95 and it'll show recommended batching window and whether expected utilization meets that. for checkout-assistant the recommended is tiny windows (20-30ms) and smaller batch sizes; net effect: Dedicated still gives cost benefits if traffic is high enough, but not if traffic is extremely spiky and low qps.
[06:23] Li Chen: do you support model pinning per-route? we sometimes want to use a larger model for certain customers.
[06:30] Priya Nair: Yes, routes can pin model versions and have rollout policies — canary percentages, fallbacks. console shows per-route rollout history.
[06:41] Dana Ortiz: about billing — how granular are invoices? our accounting wants per-team breakdown.
[06:48] Jordan Lee: Hosted bills per-token per-customer with route metadata available for PO reconciliation. Dedicated invoices have reservation charges + usage adjustments; we can produce a per-route amortized report for internal chargeback.
[07:05] [07:05] Speaker 1: (brief lag)
[07:14] Priya Nair: i'll pull up the 'Cost Explorer' view — it groups by route, model, and deployment mode. you can also tag routes for chargeback. here's an example view: top 10 routes by cost, and hover shows the cost drivers: tokens, model footprint, quantization baseline.
[07:35] Samir Patel: can you backtest what would have happened last quarter if we'd been on Dedicated with our current traffic?
[07:42] Priya Nair: yes that's the 'what-if' report. you point it at a date range and we simulate capacity configs, quantization choices, and batching. it outputs projected spend and expected p95 latency.
[07:58] Li Chen: are custom quantization profiles supported? we use int8 with some manual tuning.
[08:05] Priya Nair: we support custom quant profiles, and our onboard team can help test. the console will show expected throughput lift and any potential quality delta from evals.
[08:20] Jordan Lee: i'd like to call out the 'Alerts' tab — you can set regression alerts tied to eval sets or route-level latency/cost thresholds. when a prompt set shows a quality drop we send a regression signal.
[08:35] Samir Patel: that sounds useful. our product team wants to avoid silent regressions when model rollouts change behavior.
[08:43] Priya Nair: exactly — we integrate evals and can attach them to rollout policies so a canary doesn't promote if eval score drops.
[08:54] [08:54] Speaker 1: (typing sounds)
[09:05] Dana Ortiz: quick question on data residency — some of our customer transcripts must stay in EU. can you ensure hosting region mapping by route?
[09:15] Jordan Lee: Yes, routing policies allow region pinning per-route. we can also do private deployments with VPC options if you need on-prem.
[09:26] Samir Patel: for pilot scope, we'd like to run the checkout-assistant and returns-assistant routes. can you show what the console would look like with our traffic?
[09:35] Priya Nair: if you share two weeks of anonymized logs we can load them into the 'what-if' tool and produce a tailored cost report.
[09:44] Li Chen: what's the expected turnaround for that analysis?
[09:47] Jordan Lee: typically 3-5 business days once we have the data.
[09:52] [09:52] Speaker 1: (background noise)
[10:00] Priya Nair: i'm going to demo the CSV export for route-level cost. (clicks) you can pick date range, route tags, and include simulated Dedicated columns. export completes and you can see columns: route_id, date, requests, avg_tokens, cost_hosted, cost_dedicated_est.
[10:20] Dana Ortiz: great — finance will love that.
[10:26] Samir Patel: procurement question — what's the minimum committed capacity for Dedicated?
[10:31] Jordan Lee: our typical starting point is a 3-month reserved pool for smaller pilots, or annual for full commitments. minimum GPU count depends on model size; we can provide example configurations in the proposal.
[10:45] Li Chen: if we go Dedicated and then need to scale quickly, do you support burst to Hosted?
[10:52] Priya Nair: Yes, smart routing can burst to Hosted or other regions automatically as a fallback to preserve latency SLOs. we surface that in the console routing policy view.
[11:05] Samir Patel: any red flags from security perspective for us? we need SOC2, ISO and a KMS/HSM integration.
[11:14] Jordan Lee: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation. we support bring-your-own-KMS and can integrate with HSMs for key wrapping; Priya will share the security PDF and network diagram.
[11:28] [11:28] Speaker 1: (laptop fan noise)
[11:36] Priya Nair: quick aside — observability: trace links show token-level spans so you can trace a slow request down to model, data prep or network. that helps with SLO debug.
[11:50] Dana Ortiz: do you keep logs for how long? retention policy?
[11:54] Priya Nair: default retention is 90 days in the console, with add-on longer retention options. logs can be exported to your S3 for long-term archival.
[12:07] Samir Patel: okay next let's talk about pricing ROI. can you run a sample for checkout-assistant?
[12:15] Priya Nair: sure — switching to cost explorer, selecting Route: checkout-assistant; here's the historical spend last 30 days on Hosted: approx $4,200. projected on Dedicated with current traffic, int8 quant, and 75% utilization it's $1,600 amortized. note the model mapping we used is rdx-7b-int8 equivalent.
[12:40] Li Chen: that 2.6k delta assumes 75% utilization — our busiest windows are high but overnight is low; will that skew the economics?
[12:50] Priya Nair: yes low utilization hurts. we show a utilization sensitivity chart — if you bump to 45% the gap narrows. also you can enable auto-burst to Hosted for off-peak to avoid wasted reservation cost.
[13:07] [13:07] Speaker 1: (short interruption)
[13:20] Samir Patel: any examples of customers already using per-route chargeback?
[13:25] Jordan Lee: several retailers use route tags to allocate costs to product teams; we also provide an API to pull per-route amortized cost into your internal billing system.
[13:36] Dana Ortiz: do you provide contract language for chargeback?
[13:40] Jordan Lee: we can include an appendix with reporting SLAs and export formats in the contract.
[13:48] Li Chen: are there any gotchas with model fallbacks? if a pinned model is unavailable does it fail open to Hosted?
[13:55] Priya Nair: you configure fallback policies: failover to a compatible variant, downgrade to a smaller model, or return an error. console shows the last failover events.
[14:10] Samir Patel: for the pilot, the deliverables we want: tailored cost report for two weeks of data, security pack, and a tech kickoff to test routing and latency.
[14:20] Jordan Lee: noted — we'll produce a pilot proposal with those items.
[14:26] [14:26] Speaker 1: (keyboard)
[14:35] Priya Nair: quick demo of the 'what-if' report output — it has a PDF export with charts: route-level cost, projected latency, and a recommendation to move X% of traffic to Dedicated. you can also attach eval results.
[14:55] Dana Ortiz: timeline for pilot contract? we need procurement sign-off asap.
[15:00] Jordan Lee: we'll aim to send a draft by Monday 2026-11-15. procurement can review and propose redlines.
[15:08] Li Chen: any immediate blockers from our side? I think we need to anonymize logs before sending.
[15:14] Samir Patel: yes we'll scrub PII, but include route IDs and token counts.
[15:20] Jordan Lee: perfect. Priya, i'll hand it to you for the remaining details.
[15:25] Priya Nair: two final notes: 1) console has a cost-optimization tab with recommended quantization and batching for each route; 2) we recently added a per-prompt eval marker to catch quality regressions when enabling int8.
[15:40] Samir Patel: good to know.
[15:44] Alex (Procurement): for minimum terms — is there a pilot contract or do we sign the standard rider?
[15:49] Jordan Lee: we have a pilot addendum that keeps commitment small; i'll include that.
[15:54] [15:54] Speaker 1: (murmur)
[16:02] Jordan Lee: ok let's recap next steps: we will send pricing & pilot proposal, Priya will share SOC2 and security docs, Novaretail to send two weeks anonymized route traffic, schedule a 2-hour tech kickoff week of 2026-11-22.
[16:18] Samir Patel: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[16:22] Li Chen: thanks.
[16:25] Dana Ortiz: thanks Jordan, Priya.
[16:30] Jordan Lee: great, talk soon bye.

End of transcript. Some transcription artifacts: speaker labels approximate; minor mis-words like 'K-V cash' for KV cache, 'Kuburnates' for Kubernetes in one spot (not shown), and occasional timestamp drift.
